definition: Circumlocution means indirect and wordy language that avoids the point.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word circumlocution. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know circumlocution should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Ask Grandpa to borrow the truck and the circumlocution begins: twenty minutes on weather, tires, and responsibility, with never a yes or a no in it.
Hedging is far milder than circumlocution — a few maybes and mostlys around an answer that does, eventually, arrive; circumlocution keeps talking and never lets the answer arrive at all.
Stonewalling goes further than circumlocution — circumlocution at least keeps talking around the point; stonewalling refuses to discuss it at all.

Wordiness is simply too many words, anywhere, for any reason — a writer who cannot cut, a speaker in love with his own voice. Circumlocution is wordiness with a motive: the extra words exist to keep circling a point the speaker is dodging on purpose.

Evasion is the dodge itself, managed by any means at all — changing the subject, going silent, leaving the room. Circumlocution is one particular method of evasion: dodging with language, keeping the words flowing around the question so the answer never has to arrive.

The eighth graders wanted one fact: was the spring trip to the capital canceled or not?
The principal's Friday newsletter ran nine hundred words.
It thanked the bus company, saluted 'the flexibility of our community' at length, and reviewed the history of the trip since 1998.
It was, the student paper wrote acidly, a masterpiece of circumlocution — every sentence circling the one question and not one sentence answering it.
Two more newsletters followed, warmer and longer.
Parents began joking that the word 'canceled' must have been banned from the building.
When the announcement finally came, in April, it took eleven words.
The trip was off, and everyone had known for weeks.
